Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Nexus CleanTech Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Johnson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Nexus CleanTech's results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Elena Vargas, Chief Sustainability Officer; and Tom Reilly, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Nexus CleanTech delivered exceptional results in the third quarter, showcasing our leadership in the renewable energy sector. Our success is attributable to our innovative technologies, strategic partnerships, and unwavering commitment to sustainability.

Today, I want to highlight seven key aspects of our performance. First, our operating capacity expanded to 15.8 gigawatts, with generation output reaching 10.2 terawatt-hours, reflecting strong execution across solar, wind, and storage. Second, we secured 1.4 gigawatts of new power purchase agreements at a blended average price of $35 per megawatt-hour, bolstering our backlog. Third, capital expenditures and operating expenses demonstrated disciplined scaling, with $285 million in capex and $162 million in opex underscoring our efficiency. Fourth, gross margins improved to 28.5% and operating margins to 12.3%, driven by cost deflation and yield ramps. Fifth, government incentives contributed 28% to our adjusted EBITDA, fueled by IRA tax credits and global programs. Sixth, tax equity and project-level financings closed at $1.2 billion and $2.1 billion respectively, optimizing our capital stack. And seventh, capital recycling through asset sales generated $850 million in proceeds, redeploying into high-return development.

Now, I'll hand over the call to Michael Rivera to provide a detailed review of our financial results.

Michael Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah. Our financial performance in the third quarter was outstanding. Revenue reached $450 million, representing a 35% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by significant project commissioning and increased energy production. Our gross margin expanded to 32%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and cost management. Operating expenses totaled $162 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $85 million, or $0.72 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are raising our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

Let me expand on some of these drivers, starting with our capital expenditures, or capex, and operating expenses, or opex, which highlight our disciplined approach to scaling amid favorable tailwinds like the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act, Europe's REPowerEU plan, and accelerating global demand for energy storage. For the third quarter, we deployed $285 million in capex, bringing our nine-month trailing total to $820 million—a 28% year-over-year increase, but strategically aligned with our full-year guidance of $1.1 to $1.2 billion. This reflects our aggressive expansion into utility-scale solar PV, onshore wind hybridization, and long-duration energy storage systems to capture grid stability premiums in wholesale markets.

Breaking it down, 62% of third quarter capex, or $177 million, went to project development and EPC, including mechanical completion of our 450 megawatt-dc Gemini Solar-plus-Storage project in Nevada. It leverages high-efficiency TOPCon bifacial modules from strategic supplier partnerships, similar to those used by First Solar and LONGi, paired with 200 megawatt-hours of Tesla Megapack batteries. We're on track for commercial operations in the first quarter of 2025, with a levelized cost of energy of $28 per megawatt-hour, beating internal hurdles thanks to IRA Section 45X manufacturing credits. Battery storage and grid integration took 24%, or $68 million, accelerating deployments of our proprietary vanadium redox flow batteries in partnership with Invinity Energy Systems, targeting four-hour discharge for frequency regulation. A key initiative is our 100 megawatt/400 megawatt-hour hybrid facility in Texas' ERCOT market, where ancillary service revenues spiked 15% quarter-over-quarter due to data center load growth from hyperscalers like Google and Microsoft. The remaining 14%, or $40 million, funded expansions at our Arizona thin-film cadmium telluride panel factory, mirroring First Solar's model, and perovskite-silicon tandem cell pilots to derisk supply chains from China, where polysilicon prices stabilized at $8 per kilogram. Regionally, 55% is U.S.-focused, unlocking $12 billion in ITC and PTC transferability; 30% in Europe, chasing Germany's EEG auctions and the UK's CfD Round 5 for offshore wind; and 15% in APAC, including a 300 megawatt solar EPC contract in India's Rajasthan desert, where module costs fell 12% year-over-year to $0.22 per watt-peak.

Looking ahead, we expect fourth quarter capex of $280 to $320 million, skewed toward storage for rising firm capacity mandates. Over the next 24 months, our $3.5 billion development pipeline—1.8 gigawatts solar, 800 megawatts wind, and 2.5 gigawatt-hours storage—positions us for 25% compound annual growth in contracted backlog, akin to NextEra Energy Resources.

Turning to opex, we delivered $162 million in the third quarter, flat quarter-over-quarter but down 8% year-over-year on a per-megawatt basis, showing operating leverage from our 2.1 gigawatt global portfolio at 95% contracted under long-term PPAs and CfDs averaging 15-year terms at $45 per megawatt-hour blended. Operations and maintenance was 48%, or $78 million, 4% below guidance due to drone-based predictive maintenance and AI-driven fault detection via our NexusAI platform, powered by Siemens Gamesa tech, reducing unplanned downtime to 1.2% versus the industry average of 2.5%. Wind farm turbine servicing in our 350 megawatt U.K. portfolio benefited from blade-leading-edge erosion fixes, cutting costs 10% year-over-year. SG&A was 28%, or $45 million, disciplined at 12% of revenues, down from 15% last year, thanks to headcount optimization and synergies from our 2023 EuroWind Energy O&M acquisition, realizing $15 million annually. R&D and corporate took 24%, or $39 million, with $12 million on solid-state battery prototypes with QuantumScape for 10-hour LDES and $8 million on floating offshore wind anchors for North Sea projects. Opex intensity has declined 22% since 2022, driven by scale and hedging 85% of euro and GBP exposures. U.S. assets saw opex per megawatt-hour drop to $4.20 from $5.10 year-over-year, while Europe faced 3% inflation from EU ETS, mitigated by green H2 blending pilots.

For full-year 2024, we guide opex to $650 to $675 million, implying 5-7% growth but only 2% on adjusted EBITDA. Into 2025, we target sub-10% of revenues through automation and vertical integration.

On gross margins, we hit a non-GAAP 28.5% in the third quarter, up 320 basis points year-over-year from 25.2% and 110 basis points sequentially. Trailing twelve-month gross margins are 27.8%, a 450 basis point expansion. This stems from supply chain deflation—polysilicon down 45% to $8.5 per kilogram—benefiting our N-type TOPCon production at 85% of output. Vertical integration in silver paste and frames shaved 1.2 percentage points off costs per watt, with 95% domestic content qualifying for full IRA credits, adding $0.07 to $0.10 per watt. We've transitioned 70% of capacity to 210 millimeter wafer TOPCon lines at 22.8% efficiency, reducing bill of materials 15% year-over-year and improving cell-to-module ratios to 98.5%. Fab 3 in Arizona hit 95% utilization. U.S. sales at 65% of revenue saw 31.2% margins from utility-scale PPAs; Europe 25.8% despite $0.24 per watt ASPs; APAC 22.1%. We guide Q4 gross margins to 29-30% and full-year to 28.2%.

Operating margins came in at 12.3% non-GAAP, up 220 basis points year-over-year. OpEx as a percentage of revenue fell to 16.2%, with R&D at 4.8% funding HJT pilots and hydrogen electrolyzers targeting $1.50 per kilogram H2 by 2026, and SG&A efficiency up 25%. For 2025, with Fab 4's 2 gigawatt ramp, we see gross margins toward 32%+.

Government incentives and subsidies were pivotal, contributing 28% to adjusted EBITDA, up from 22% year-over-year. U.S. operations captured $285 million in tax equity via IRA ITC and PTC—for 1.2 gigawatts solar, a 42% blended ITC boosting IRRs to 12-14%; wind added $112 million. Grants included $75 million from DOE for our Nevada gigafactory. Section 45X yielded $45 million year-to-date from Arizona panels. BESS ITC at 30-50% accelerated 2.4 gigawatt-hours; EU Innovation Fund $130 million for Dutch hybrids; green H2 45V at $3 per kilogram. U.S. IRA deployed $110 billion year-to-date; Europe REPowerEU €45 billion; India PLI 2.0 for 2 gigawatts. We've raised FY24 EBITDA guidance to $1.65-1.75 billion, with subsidies 65% of the uplift.

Tax equity financing funded 40-60% of U.S. stacks, closing $1.2 billion across eight projects like Desert Bloom's $180 million at 8.2% investor IRR. IRA transferability cut discounts to 5%. Project-level debt hit $2.1 billion at 4.8%, including $650 million green bonds for Horizon BESS and ECA support for offshore wind. Our WACC is 5.2-5.8%, with $15 billion queued capital.

Capital recycling generated $850 million in Q3 from SunVista solar sale at 11.5x EBITDA and a Midwest wind stake at 10.8x. Year-to-date $2.7 billion across 1.2 gigawatts, 65% redeployed to pipeline, 25% deleveraging net debt-to-EBITDA to 3.8x. U.S. cap rates compressed to 5.5-6.5%; Europe rebounding with North Sea sales. Target $3.5-4 billion in 2024.

I'll now turn the call over to Lisa Chen to discuss our project development activities.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Michael. Our project development pipeline continues to expand, with 5 gigawatts of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. We are making excellent progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. Securing high-quality, long-duration PPAs provides revenue visibility and shields us from merchant volatility. In Q3, we secured 1.4 gigawatts of new PPAs, bringing total contracted backlog to 8.2 gigawatts—up 45% year-over-year. Highlights include a 750 megawatt solar-plus-storage hybrid with a Big Tech off-taker for Gemini Solar at $42 per megawatt-hour levelized, bundling 550 megawatts-dc TOPCon with 800 megawatt-hours LFP storage. Also, a 450 megawatt wind PPA for Rattlesnake Ridge at $28 per megawatt-hour with Siemens Gamesa turbines. 60% U.S.-based, 40% Europe and APAC like Germany's €45 per megawatt-hour and India's $29 per megawatt-hour. Blended new PPA price $35 per megawatt-hour, down 8% year-over-year from LCOE compression, but hybrids at $48 per megawatt-hour up 12%. Q4 auctions signal $38-45 floors from data center RFPs. These support $1.2 billion tax equity and 2.5 gigawatts construction starts in 2025.

We expect several new projects online soon, further contributing to revenue. We're pursuing acquisitions to accelerate growth.

Dr. Raj Patel, can you update us on technological advancements?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. We are dedicated to driving innovation. Our R&D focuses on advanced solar panels like TOPCon bifacial and perovskite tandems, energy storage including VRFBs and solid-state prototypes with QuantumScape, and smart grid tech. Breakthroughs in HJT at 25.5% efficiency, floating offshore anchors, and AI platforms like NexusAI enhance reliability and affordability, positioning us to transform the energy landscape with LCOE improvements for 2030.

Next, Elena will discuss sustainability initiatives.

Elena Vargas:
Thank you, Raj. Sustainability is core at Nexus CleanTech. We're minimizing environmental impact with goals for carbon reductions, energy efficiency, and resource management. Our incentives stacking—IRA 45X, EU funds, green H2 PTC—aligns with community engagement and local initiatives, powering a sustainable future.

Now, Tom will provide operational highlights.

Tom Reilly:
Thank you, Elena. Our operational performance remains strong. Operating capacity stood at 15.8 gigawatts end of Q3, up 22% year-over-year from 12.9 gigawatts: 8.4 gigawatts solar (53%), 4.9 gigawatts onshore wind (31%), 1.7 gigawatts offshore (11%), 800 megawatts BESS. North America 68%, Europe 22%, APAC 10%. Generation output hit 10.2 terawatt-hours, up 18% year-over-year: solar 4.8 TWh at 26.5% capacity factor, onshore wind 3.1 TWh at 32%, offshore 1.6 TWh at 48%, BESS 0.7 TWh. Above-average weather, diversification—45% PPAs, 30% merchant—and hybrids drive resilience. Q3 guidance 12.8 TWh. We're optimizing with predictive maintenance, supply chain de-risking, and training.

I'll turn it back to Sarah for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Tom. To summarize, Nexus CleanTech had an exceptional third quarter. We are confident our strategic initiatives, innovation commitment, and sustainability focus will drive continued growth.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will open the floor for questions. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
What are your plans for expanding your presence in international markets?

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks, John. International expansion is a key pillar, with 40% of our new PPAs outside the U.S., including Germany, UK, India, and Australia. We're leveraging REPowerEU in Europe for offshore wind auctions, PLI in India for 2 gigawatts modules, and Australia's Capacity Investment Scheme. Our APAC solar EPC and LatAm recycling build momentum. With $3.5 billion pipeline diversified, we target 25% CAGR, prioritizing hybrids and local partnerships to navigate permitting and grids while capturing $1.2 trillion global capex.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
How are you addressing the challenge of intermittency associated with renewable energy sources?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Great question, Maria. Intermittency is core to our innovation. Our hybrids—solar-plus-storage like Gemini with 800 MWh LFP or VRFBs for four-hour firming—deliver 24/7 power, commanding 25-30% PPA premiums. NexusAI optimizes dispatch, reducing curtailment; BESS captures ancillary revenues up 15% in ERCOT. Offshore wind at 48% factors and green H2 pilots stack with 45V credits. 60% of pipeline is hybrid, targeting 50%+ fleet factors, de-risking via FERC changes and IRA stacking.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
Can you discuss the impact of government subsidies and tax incentives on your profitability?

Michael Rivera:
Absolutely, David. Subsidies drove 28% of Q3 EBITDA, up from 22%, via $285 million IRA ITC/PTC, $45 million 45X, DOE grants shielding polysilicon rises and boosting margins 420 bps to 32.4%. Stacking domestic content (10%), energy communities (10%), and BESS ITC expanded IRRs 400 bps. Europe REPowerEU, India PLI add uplift; 75% U.S. chain IRA-compliant. Even with risks like PTC phase-outs, bipartisan support and hedging sustain 18-22% EBITDA CAGR.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
What are your expectations for electricity demand growth in the coming years?

Sarah Thompson:
Emily, demand growth is explosive from data centers—100 gigawatts U.S. hyperscaler pipeline—and electrification. We see 4-5% annual U.S. growth per EIA, accelerated by AI to 8-10%. Our PPAs with Big Tech at $42/MWh capture this; hybrids meet firming mandates. Global $1.7 trillion clean tech spend positions our 25 gigawatt pipeline for outsized growth, with backlog implying $450 million EBITDA in 2025.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time there appear to be no further questions. I will now turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for any closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of Nexus CleanTech. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
